chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The woman is returned (from the dowry/marriage contract) for four conditions: vitiligo, leprosy, insanity, and uterine horns (Al-Qaran), which is inability to copulate (Al-Afal), as long as it has not fallen upon her (i.e., the husband has not consummated the marriage with her). So when it has fallen upon her, then no (she is not returned).

key_terms.الْبَرَصُ: Vitiligo (a skin disease causing loss of color)
key_terms.الْعَفَلُ: Inability to copulate due to physical obstruction

ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions in a woman that allow for marriage annulment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes the principle of 'gharar' (deception) in marriage contracts, allowing for annulment if specific defects—vitiligo, leprosy, insanity, and uterine horns (qaran)—are concealed and discovered before consummation. The condition 'if it has not fallen upon her' implies that once the husband has engaged in sexual intercourse, the defect is considered accepted, and the right to return the dowry is forfeited, reflecting the legal concept of 'iqab' (acceptance). This ruling underscores the importance of transparency in marital agreements within the Imami tradition.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhamma Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, having said:

‘The woman would be returned from four things – from the vitiligo, and the leprosy, and the insanity, and the uterine horns, and it is Al Afal (inability to copulate due to uterine horns), for as long as he has not fallen upon her. So when he falls upon her, so no’.
en.sarwar: 16. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

A woman can be returned because of four things: al- Bars (albino, a form of leprosy), leprosy, insanity and al-Qarn which is al-‘Afal, (growth of a substance in her vagina that prevents sexual intercourse) if he has not yet gone to bed with her, and if so then she cannot be returned.’”
